overview.title: Your frameworks in one place
overview.body: Each card is a standard or regulation your organisation works towards. The ring shows readiness: how much of the framework is covered by evidence you have linked, and how recent that evidence is.
overview.step1: Enable the frameworks that are in scope. Start with the ones your customers or regulators ask about.
overview.step2: Open a framework to assess each requirement: mark what does not apply and link documents or deviations as evidence.
overview.step3: Use Readiness details to see what is missing, and keep evidence up to date so the score stays high.
overview.why: Management system standards ask you to plan, implement and show evidence. Clauses 4 to 10 share one structure across ISO standards, so one well-kept record often serves several frameworks at once.

readiness.title: What the readiness score tells you
readiness.body: The score summarises how prepared you are for an audit or a regulator's review. It only counts requirements you have marked as applicable.
readiness.step1: Look at the red segment first: requirements nobody has started on.
readiness.step2: Then refresh evidence older than a year. Auditors expect records to be current.
readiness.step3: Open the standard to link evidence, or ask for a summary of what to do next.
readiness.why: ISO standards require you to monitor and evaluate your management system and review it at management level. A readiness score per framework is a simple input to that review.

readiness.title: How readiness is calculated
readiness.s1Body: When a requirement does not apply to you, mark it as not applicable and write a short justification. It then leaves the calculation, so the score reflects what you actually have to do.
readiness.s2Body: A requirement is covered when you have confirmed at least one live record as evidence, or set the status to covered yourself. A partly covered requirement counts half.
readiness.s3Body: Evidence confirmed or updated within the last 365 days counts in full. Older evidence counts 60%, because auditors expect records to be kept up to date.
readiness.question: You cover a requirement with a procedure last reviewed two years ago. How much does it count?
readiness.explanation: It is still covered, but the evidence is older than a year, so it counts 60%. Review the procedure to make it count in full again.
